change.title: pr-36882-flat
change.description: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: "The Operator will fail" is not backed by operator code
findings.body: The CAUTION says that without `rolling-updates` "the Keycloak Operator will fail". Nothing under `operator/src/main` checks for this feature: `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` (operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) picks a logic from `update.strategy` alone, and a search of `operator/src/main` for `Profile` or `rolling-updates` finds no feature check. The Operator also never invokes `update-compatibility` (no `compatib*` match in `operator/src`). A CR with `update.strategy: Recreate` and no feature will probably be reconciled as before. Say what actually happens, for example that the preview strategy support requires the feature. If the Operator is supposed to reject such a CR, that check is missing from this PR.

findings.title: setEnabledFeatures replaces any features already on the CR, and the null-strategy case never enables the feature
findings.body: `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...))` overwrites any `features.enabled` list that `getTestKeycloakDeployment` may have set. Add to the existing list instead of replacing it. Also, the early `return kc` at line 106 skips the feature for the `null` strategy case. That is consistent with the docs, but it means the default (not set) path is only tested with the feature off, even though the custom image in `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` is now built with it. Confirm that this is intended.

contracts.action: `update-compatibility check` and `update-compatibility metadata` now exit early when the `rolling-updates` preview feature is disabled
contracts.equivalent_path: UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run does the same, and the same method already ends with picocli.exit(result.exitCode()) for the normal result.
contracts.before_after: Before: the commands ran for everyone, with a preview warning. After: the feature check runs first, so printPreviewWarning, validateConfig and the compatibility logic are skipped. The command prints the error to stderr and exits with code 4.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled.' on stderr and gets exit code 4. UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled (lines 46-50) covers the message.
contracts.failure_mode: If `--file` is missing and the feature is off, the user gets the feature error and never reaches the 'Missing required argument' validation. This is acceptable.

contracts.action: Exit codes changed: recreate upgrade 4 -> 3, new FEATURE_DISABLED = 4
contracts.equivalent_path: IncompatibleResult.exitCode returns CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, so it follows the constant. The docs table in update-compatibility.adoc already listed 3 for recreate.
contracts.before_after: Before: the code returned 4 for recreate while the docs said 3. After: the code returns 3, which matches the docs, and 4 means the feature is disabled.
contracts.visible_effect: Scripts that checked for exit code 4 as 'recreate needed' now see 3. Exit code 4 now means the feature is off. Since the command is preview, this is acceptable.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. No other caller hardcodes 4: the grep found only the constants and IncompatibleResult.

summary: The change gates `update-compatibility check` and `metadata` behind a new `ROLLING_UPDATES` preview feature, and the code looks correct. The recreate exit code moves from 4 to 3, which matches the existing docs table. I found no other caller that hardcodes 4. Two minor items remain. First, the Operator docs say the Operator will fail without the feature, but I found no Operator code that checks it. Second, the Operator test replaces any features already on the CR, and it enables the feature only when a strategy is set.
